newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Sentrachem to post half year loss.
newsitem.headline: Sentrachem to post half year loss.

text.p: South African chemical firm Sentrachem Ltd said on Wednesday that it would post a loss for the first half to February 28 after taking one-off charges worth a total of 261 million rand at its Sanachem unit.

The firm has launched a major restructuring of Sanachem's businesses and will charge 144 million rand after tax and provisions to cover a reduction in Sanachem's product range, the cancelling of registrations of uneconomic products and a review of market conditions.

Another charge of 117 million rand will be taken as a result of unrealitisic forward exchange contracts. That charge was announced last NovEmber and at the time Sentrachem warned it was urgently reviewing its group profit forecasts.

Sentrachem managing director John Job said the rest of the group is performing well. "Sanachem's problems have obviously overshadowed the performance of the rest of the group, which is otherwise in fine shape," he said in a statement.
Sentrachem's Hampshire Chemical, Karbochem and Safripol units are all showing substantial growth, while its NCP subsidiary is slightly down, but still profitable.
"With profits in these companies skewed towards the second half, prospects in that period look substantially better than in the firt half," he said.
Sentrachem's plans for Sanachem include a reduction in products and a focus on core markets.
"I am confident that the new stratgey for Sanachem is sound. Having decided to clean the slate by taking all the write-offs up front, the company should return to profitabilty next year," he said.
The news was announced just after the local share market had closed. Sentrachem shares ended the day down four cents at 844 cents.
